summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a recent stump revision was admitted for fever, abdominal pain, and lethargy. She was found to have leukocytosis, acute kidney injury, and hyperkalemia. Initial concerns included pneumonia and possible C. difficile, but the source of infection was confirmed as a urinary tract infection caused by carbapenem-resistant ESBL Klebsiella. She was treated with intravenous meropenem and vancomycin, then transitioned to colistin after culture results. Her infection resolved, renal function normalized, and blood pressure stabilized with adjustment of metoprolol. She remained in the hospital for clinical observation until her father returned to assist at home, as she declined rehabilitation. She was discharged on home health for colistin administration, with stable vital signs and improving lab values.
